rationale: B is more useful because it gives a sharper recommendation with explicit decision triggers: choose personalized shareability plus partnerships, but swap in load-time work if mobile performance is poor, or platform-native formats if partnerships are unrealistic. Its comparative reasoning is more discriminative, especially around why identity-driven sharing outperforms plain customization. It also handles uncertainty better by naming concrete failure modes and feasibility constraints. A is solid and practical, but B’s conditional guidance, stronger mechanism-level reasoning, and more decision-relevant caveats make it more helpful to a careful decision-maker.
